The override is still used, never rejected.

DESKTOP-071Settings › Inventory. Locations and their areas, behind the Inventory registers (8a). A location is anything whose contents are kept as one register: a house, a storage unit, a car, a boat. Drawn like Categories (DESKTOP-068): one LOCATIONS list, NAME only, each location in 800 with a muted “n areas · n items” note and its areas indented under it, in area-tab order; the disclosure collapses a location (Storage unit and Hilux shown collapsed). Address and insurance cover are not set up here: they live on the register in Inventory (8a), and Add/Edit location asks only for the name and Unit. The Units table principles (DESKTOP-065): no ACTIONS column, the square + beside LOCATIONS adds a location, double-click a row to edit it, and right-click for its context menu. A location's menu reads Add area… (works collapsed too, and expands it) · Edit location… · Remove location…; a adds an area to the selected location. Drawn here: Office right-clicked, with Edit area…, Move up, Move down and Remove area….

DESKTOP-139Edit unit — btc, with the PRICE SOURCE group that links a unit to a source. The symbol belongs to this link, not to the source: CoinGecko knows btc as bitcoin, Yahoo Finance would know vas as VAS.AX. Quoted in defaults to the base unit. Choosing Manual entry hides Symbol, Quoted in and Test. Add unit is the same form, empty, with the source set to Manual entry.

DESKTOP-136Add price source, Custom… — a source the app doesn't ship. The address, a request template and a price path are stored as separate fields, never one long URL, so a unit's symbol and the API key are never baked in. The key is stored in the OS keychain on this device and never syncs; the Ledger holds only the name of the parameter it goes in. Test asks for a symbol because the source itself has none.
